g.title: ALNS
g.text: ALNS — Adaptive Large Neighbourhood Search (Ropke & Pisinger 2006)

Destroy q nodes, repair with an insertion heuristic, accept via a pluggable criterion (default simulated annealing), and learn operator weights per segment from scores σ₁/σ₂/σ₃. Objective: maximise profit = R·Σ waste − C·Σ distance under capacity and mandatory coverage.

g.title: a_params
g.text: Load capacity, R, C · build sub-problem (all bins if vrpp)
regret_pool regret234, σ₁ 33 / σ₂ 9 / σ₃ 13, acceptance criterion

g.title: a_map
g.text: map local routes → global tour · km on full matrix

g.title: i_repair
g.text: REPAIR registry: Greedy, Regret-2 (+ Regret-3, Regret-4 for regret234)
+ Savings; each noise-capable op expanded into Clean and Noisy slots

g.title: m_init
g.text: best = current · profit = R·Σ waste − C·km

g.title: m_temp
g.text: dynamic T₀: accept a start_temp_control (5 %) worse

g.title: m_seg
g.text: w_i ← (1 − r)·w_i + r · π_i / θ_i for used ops

g.title: d_noise
g.text: noise = U(−η·d_max, +η·d_max) if selected repair slot is Noisy, else 0

g.title: d_destroy
g.text: Random: uniform picks · Worst: highest saving, randomised by p
Shaw: relatedness (distance, load), randomised by p_shaw
String / Cluster / Neighbor: spatially contiguous removals

g.title: d_repair
g.text: Greedy: cheapest insertion · Regret-k: max (kth best − best) first
Savings: Clarke-Wright merge · mandatory nodes always inserted;
optional nodes only if profitable (VRPP); capacity respected
